extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency administrators (e.g., NFAC administrative staff, OMB officials) responsible for designing/implementing employee parking charge policies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and implementing an OMB circular or agency policy on charging employees for parking at Headquarters and similar federal buildings, balancing energy conservation goals with fairness for employees lacking transit or working irregular hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess availability of public transportation before imposing charges
rubrics_metrics.description: First... is the lack of adequate public transportation available not only from places such as West Virginia where many of our employees live but from a great many areas in northern Virginia and Maryland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let lack of adequate public transportation result in a financial penalty to federal employees. Although OMB suggests resolving this through discussions with transit companies, there is no assurance of a favorable resolution — the availability of transit must be assessed and taken into account before imposing parking charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive charges for employees without transit or carpool options
rubrics_metrics.description: Those without access to adequate public transportation and unable to locate or form a carpool should not be made to pay an excessive parking charge in addition to the high cost of operating a vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many prefer to drive. Consider that intensive surveys may show employees would stop driving alone if provided reasonably scheduled transit or carpools. Therefore set charges so as not to impose undue financial burden on those lacking alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for employees working irregular hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Another group mentioned for special attention are those people who work irregular hours. Many people in OER would fall into this category and rarely if ever would they be able to utilize public transportation or join car pools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It would be unfair to penalize irregular-hours workers financially for something not under their control. Consider alternatives such as paying an additional sum for demands made by their job rather than charging an excessive parking fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use positive incentives and transit arrangements rather than punitive large fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Since energy conservation is the primary goal in this exercise and the utilization of car pools and mass transportation systems is being urged to accomplish this goal, perhaps a more positive approach to the problem should be taken rather than the negative one suggested by large parking fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor programs that facilitate carpooling and mass transit (e.g., guaranteed bus service from fringe parking areas) over simply raising parking fees to discourage driving. Design policy tools to encourage voluntary modal shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct employee surveys to inform transit/service decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A survey should be conducted to determine those willing to routinely take a bus to and from work and then establish with the transit company a guaranteed number of passengers between particularly well-populated points (fringe parking areas) and the Headquarters building for instance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey data to negotiate service levels with transit companies and to identify feasible routes/times that would attract habitual riders (particularly for routine eight-hour workers). Surveys can also show latent demand and clarify who truly lacks alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish fringe parking and guaranteed transit services for routine schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish with the transit company a guaranteed number of passengers between particularly well-populated points (fringe parking areas) and the Headquarters building... This would provide adequate service for those who work a routine eight hour day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create fringe parking areas with coordinated bus service to headquarters for employees on routine schedules, as a practical measure to reduce single-occupancy driving and meet energy conservation goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply minimal parking charges at Headquarters and similar buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: One way or the other in the draft circular and its attachment, several are, worth raising again if only to support a recommendation that minimal charges be applied at Headquarters and buildings with similar problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When charges are implemented at central facilities, keep them minimal to balance revenue/behavioral goals with fairness concerns; avoid excessive fees that would unduly burden employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define exemptions/fee rules for those unable to use transit services
rubrics_metrics.description: Those unable to use this service for legitimate reasons, and essentially this would mean only those in car pools or working unusual hours, would be subject to the minimum parking fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify clearly who is eligible for transit-fringe arrangements and who must pay (or is exempt from) fees. Use objective criteria (e.g., participation in car pools, irregular shifts) to determine fee application or exemptions; resolve any apparent contradictions in exemption policy so it treats carpoolers and irregular-hours workers fairly.
